note: THE WIDTH-CHANGE CONTRACT, half two, asked so the MESSAGE is the value -- both sides raise plain `error` here, so a case comparing condition symbols alone would call this an agreement and learn nothing. Emacs has two distinct refusals and they name the two directions: "Attempt to store non-byte value into unibyte string" for a codepoint above 255 into an ASCII string, and "Attempt to replace non-ASCII char in multibyte string" for any write over a multibyte character. So Emacs' `aset` never changes a string's width -- it refuses instead -- which is the property Phase 25.1's "string mutation preserves the stable header even when a codepoint-width change requires a replacement block" gate has to be read against. kg answers its own single message twice.
